cards.text: Ezekiel is a priest living among the exiles in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 1:1-3), and he's in the middle of a vision of Jerusalem. He just watched the glory of the LORD stop at the entrance of the east gate of the LORD's house (Ezekiel 10:19). Now the Spirit lifts Ezekiel up and brings him to that same gate, where twenty-five men are standing, and two of them get named: Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah.

cards.question: Jaazaniah and Pelatiah are standing at the east gate. Who are these two men?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Ezekiel. He calls him "Son of man" and tells him exactly what kind of men these twenty-five are.

cards.question: The LORD tells Ezekiel these twenty-five men give good counsel in the city.

cards.text: And here's what they're saying: 'Is not the time near to build houses? The city is the cooking pot, and we are the meat.' Twenty-five men at one gate with a SLOGAN, friend, and I lived in a junk drawer for years where the best slogan we ever came up with was "Please don't throw us out."

cards.question: So what does the LORD tell Ezekiel to do about the twenty-five leaders at the east gate?

cards.text: The Spirit of the LORD falls on Ezekiel, and God starts with what's going on inside these men's heads. You can't hide a thought from God, friend. I can't even hide a burnt batch from my own NOSE.

cards.question: God says He knows the thoughts that come up in the minds of the house of Israel.

cards.text: Then God names what they've done in this city. They've multiplied those they killed and filled its streets with the dead.

cards.question: God takes the leaders' cooking pot picture and turns it around. Who does He say the meat in the pot really is?

answers.text: The people they killed in the city
The leaders standing at the gate

cards.question: God says He will leave these leaders right where they are, inside the city.
These leaders are afraid of something, and God says that's exactly what He'll bring against them: the ___.

cards.text: God will bring them out of the city and hand them over to foreigners. They'll fall by the sword, He'll judge them even to the borders of Israel, and then, He says, they will know that He is the LORD.

cards.question: In the end, God says the city will still be a cooking pot for these leaders.
God gives His reason: these leaders haven't followed His statutes or practiced His ordinances. Instead, they've followed the ordinances of the ___ around them.

cards.text: Ezekiel is still in the middle of this message. Then something happens to Pelatiah son of Benaiah, one of the two leaders named at the gate.

cards.question: While Ezekiel is still prophesying, what happens to Pelatiah son of Benaiah?
Ezekiel falls facedown and cries out in a loud voice. What does he ask the Lord GOD?

answers.text: Will You bring the remnant of Israel to a complete end
Will You bring Pelatiah back to life again
Will You send me home to the exiles now

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel. It's about his brothers, his fellow exiles and the whole house of Israel, and what the people of Jerusalem have been saying about them.

cards.question: What have the people of Jerusalem been saying about Ezekiel's fellow exiles?

answers.text: They are far away from the LORD
They will be coming home soon
They are the true leaders now

cards.question: The people of Jerusalem also say the land has been given to them as a possession.

cards.text: But God answers back: yes, He sent them far away and scattered them among the nations. I know that out-of-sight feeling, friend, because I spent YEARS under the takeout menus.

cards.question: Far away in those countries, what does God say He has been for the exiles, for a little while?

cards.text: And then the Lord GOD makes the exiles a promise. He'll gather them from the peoples and bring them together from every country where they've been scattered.

cards.question: Once He gathers the exiles, God says He'll give back to them the ___ of Israel.
When the exiles return to the land, God says they'll leave its detestable things right where they are.

cards.text: Now we get to the heart of it, LITERALLY. God says He'll give them singleness of heart and put a new spirit within them.

cards.question: God says He'll take out one kind of heart and put in another. Which heart does He remove?
In place of the heart of stone, God gives them a heart of ___.

cards.text: Out with stone, in with flesh, and God doesn't patch up the old one, He swaps it. I know a little about that, friend: I went into that junk drawer blurry and came out SHARP, and now God says why He's doing all this.

cards.question: Why does God give the exiles a new heart and a new spirit?

answers.text: So they may follow His statutes
So they may rebuild the walls
So they may rule the nations

cards.question: God says of them, "Then they will be My people, and I will be their God."

cards.text: But there's a warning in it too. For those whose hearts pursue detestable things and abominations, God says He'll bring their conduct down on their own heads.
Then the cherubim spread their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel is above them. The glory of the LORD rises up from within the city.

cards.question: The glory of the LORD leaves the city and stands over the mountain ___ of the city.

cards.text: Then the Spirit lifts Ezekiel up and carries him back to Chaldea, to the exiles, and the vision goes up from him. One minute he's at the temple gate, the next he's home, and I've been teleported less smoothly by a drawer slamming shut.

cards.question: Back home with the exiles in Chaldea, what does Ezekiel do with this whole vision?

answers.text: He tells them everything the LORD showed him
He keeps every part of it to himself
He shares it only with the other priests

findings.problem: The card says 'You can't hide a thought from God,' which gives away the answer to card 8. Card 8 asks the baker to confirm that God knows the thoughts that come up in their minds.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card says God starts with what's going on inside 'these men's heads.' In Ezekiel 11:5, God addresses 'O house of Israel.' The card narrows who is being spoken to. Card 8 then correctly says 'the house of Israel,' so the two cards don't match.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new moment in the junk drawer: a 'slogan' the drawer friends came up with. The backstory has no such moment. Made-up moments are only allowed around his bakery.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The first six choice cards strictly alternate question types: multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false (cards 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 11). Stop 2 also opens with the same multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice sequence.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: 'Out with stone, in with flesh' restates what cards 10 and 11 just asked, and the rest of the card is a joke plus a teaser. The card tells no new piece of the passage.
The card cites Ezekiel 11:19-20, but it tells nothing from 11:20. It only says 'now God says why He's doing all this.' Verse 20 is told on cards 13 and 14.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the action. The card stresses that God doesn't patch up the old heart but swaps it. Papa Dorin's own story is a renewal: the same stamper made sharp again, not swapped out for a new one.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'I've been teleported less smoothly by a drawer slamming shut' doesn't click. A drawer slamming shut doesn't move anyone anywhere, and his backstory has no such moment. A stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
